steps.title: Touchdown signal
steps.body: When a team scores a touchdown, the referee raises both arms straight up over their head.

steps.title: First down signal
steps.body: For a first down, the referee points one arm forward, toward the end zone the offense is going to.

steps.title: Incomplete pass
steps.body: If a pass is not caught, the referee swings both arms back and forth, crossing in front of their body.

steps.prompt: Both of the referee's arms go straight up. What happened?
steps.explanation: Both arms straight up means touchdown!

steps.prompt: A referee throws a yellow flag. What does it mean?
steps.explanation: The yellow flag means a player broke a rule. The referee explains after the play.

steps.prompt: Match the signal to what it means.
steps.explanation: Learn these four and you can follow the referees in any game.

steps.title: Offside
steps.body: Before the snap, the defense must stay on its side of the line. If a defender is across the line when the ball is snapped, it is offside: 5 yards.

steps.title: Holding
steps.body: Blockers may push, but they can't grab and hold another player to stop them. That is holding, and it costs 10 yards on the offense.

steps.title: Pass interference
steps.body: When a pass is in the air, players can't push or grab to stop someone from catching it. That is pass interference.

steps.title: Delay of game
steps.body: The offense has a play clock. If it runs out before the snap, it is delay of game: 5 yards.

steps.prompt: A blocker grabs a defender's jersey to stop him. What penalty is that?
steps.explanation: Grabbing to stop a player is holding.

steps.prompt: A defender is across the line when the ball is snapped. What is it?
steps.explanation: The defense must stay on its side until the snap. Crossing early is offside.

steps.statement: If the play clock runs out before the snap, the offense loses 5 yards.
steps.explanation: Yes. That is delay of game.

steps.prompt: Match each penalty to its meaning.

pairs.right: Defense across the line at the snap
Stopping a catch by pushing or grabbing

steps.explanation: Penalties keep the game fair. Each one has its own yards.

steps.title: Timeouts
steps.body: A timeout stops the clock so a team can rest and plan. In the NFL, each team gets 3 timeouts in each half.

steps.title: When the clock stops
steps.body: The game clock stops when a pass is not caught. It also stops for timeouts, scores and penalties.

steps.prompt: In the NFL, how many timeouts does each team get in a half?
steps.explanation: Three per half. Coaches save them for the end of the half.

steps.statement: The clock stops after an incomplete pass.
steps.explanation: Yes! A pass that is not caught stops the clock.

steps.prompt: Why do teams save timeouts for the end of a half?
choices: To stop the clock when time is short
To make the game longer for fun
steps.explanation: Near the end, every second matters. A timeout saves time for one more play.

steps.statement: Kids' leagues always use exactly the same timeout rules as the NFL.
steps.explanation: Not quite. Youth and flag leagues set their own rules, so ask your coach.

steps.title: No late hits
steps.body: When the whistle blows, the play is over. Hitting a player after that is unnecessary roughness: a 15-yard penalty.

steps.title: Protect the quarterback
steps.body: Defenders may not hit the quarterback after he has thrown the ball, or hit him in the head. That's roughing the passer: 15 yards and a first down.

steps.title: Head up
steps.body: Never hit with the top of your helmet or aim at someone's head. In college football that's called targeting, and the player is sent out of the game.

steps.title: Hands off receivers
steps.body: In the NFL, once a receiver is 5 yards past the line, a defender may not push or grab him before the ball is thrown. That's illegal contact.

steps.prompt: A defender hits the quarterback after he already threw the ball. What's the call?
steps.explanation: Yes. That's 15 yards and an automatic first down.

steps.statement: It's fine to tackle a player after the whistle if he still has the ball.
steps.explanation: Not quite. After the whistle the play is over. A late hit is unnecessary roughness.

steps.prompt: Why is hitting with the top of your helmet against the rules?
choices: It can hurt the head and neck
It makes the ball fly away
steps.explanation: Yes. Keep your head up and see what you hit. In college it's targeting, and the player is sent off.

steps.statement: In the NFL, a defender may grab a receiver 20 yards downfield before the ball is thrown.
steps.explanation: Not quite. Past 5 yards, that's illegal contact: 5 yards and an automatic first down.
